subject: Thundering herd on reserved capacity — immediate mitigation & evidence request

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Liam Park <liam.park@orbittech.com>, support@orbittech.com
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Thundering herd on reserved capacity — immediate mitigation & evidence request

Liam / OrbitTech team —

Thanks for the quick sync this morning. I wanted to summarize what we observed from our side and the immediate mitigation steps we took so the record is clear ahead of the post-incident follow-up.

What happened (summary):
- 2026-10-30 08:47 PDT: sudden traffic surge to your reserved pool in us-west-2; QPS spiked ~6x baseline over ~90s.
- Sustained burst created a short-lived scheduler backlog and increased queue depth; average token latency spiked from ~60ms to ~900ms and some requests experienced tail latencies > 5s.
- Our autoscaler reacted but with warmup lag on reserved nodes; we saw eviction/retry cycles for low-priority warm workers (a partial "thundering herd" where retries amplified demand).

Immediate mitigations we applied:
- Temporarily increased reserved capacity by promoting a held warm standby set at 08:55 PDT.
- Activated cross-pool routing to a compatible backup cluster to shed a portion of the burst.
- Enabled short-lived aggressive prefix/KV cache bypass to avoid cache stampedes for new request patterns.

Current status: traffic normalized by 09:10 PDT after routing and standby promotion. No data-exfiltration or credentials exposure observed. We collected detailed telemetry and a metrics snapshot (attached).

Action items for OrbitTech (requested):
1) Can you share any release/toggle changes, rollout timestamps, or client retry policy changes around 08:30–09:00 PDT?
2) Please provide a 10-minute client-side trace covering the surge window and any retry logs.

Attachments included: metrics_snapshot_20261030.png (server-side QPS/latency), evidence_packet_orbittech_20261030.zip (prometheus/coredump slice), mitigation_runbook_v2.pdf (internal runbook changes we executed).

Proposed next steps:
- Short (30m) post-incident sync Monday 2026-11-02 at 10:00 AM PT to review traces and agree on hardening steps.
- We will prepare a preliminary root-cause hypothesis and a remediation checklist for your review before the call.

I’m looping in Camila and Ben from customer ops to coordinate credits and remediation scheduling. Kimberly is on legal/contract watch in case we need to surface an SLA credit.

Thanks —
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Thundering herd on reserved capacity — immediate mitigation & evidence request

Rafael —

Appreciate the quick remediation on your side and the write-up. We dug into our rollout timeline and confirmed a canary gate change at 08:40 PDT that unintentionally enabled aggressive client retries when a subset of our edge proxies returned 500s. That triggered repeated client attempts within ~30s windows.

We attached a small packet (attached) with our client debug logs and a snippet of the rollout config. We’re running an internal postmortem and will share the full playbook by Monday.

Two quick asks from our side:
- Do you have a recommended mitigation for client retries to avoid amplifying transient 5xx patterns?
- Can you confirm whether any requests were retried with altered headers (we need to be sure we didn’t trigger downstream duplicates in our own ingestion system)?

Thanks for looping Camila/Ben.

—Liam
Liam Park
Head of Platform Ops, OrbitTech
liam.park@orbittech.com

Liam —

Thanks for the quick confirmation and for sending the client logs. That rollout detail (08:40 canary gate) aligns with the spike window. A couple notes and recommendations from our side: 

1) Short-term mitigation for client retries: enforce exponential backoff with jitter on the client side and limit retry attempts to 2 for idempotent calls; for non-idempotent calls use a circuit-breaker at the edge. We can share a client-side snippet you can push to the rollout to gate retries.

2) About altered headers / duplicates: our telemetry shows no header rewriting on retry and we did not observe duplicate downstream ingestion from our platform during the incident window. We’ll include request-id correlation in the evidence packet to make it easier to validate.

3) Compensation / credits: We propose a 10% service credit for the impacted hour and a one-time ops time credit to support your postmortem. Camila will follow up with formal credit paperwork if that’s acceptable.

4) Post-incident sync: Confirmed proposed meeting: Mon 2026-11-02 10:00 AM PT. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda and the preliminary RCA outline.

Next: Camila — can you take point on credits and scheduling? Ben — can you coordinate an ops-oriented checklist to harden autoscaler warmup behavior for reserved pools (short-term knobs)?

Thanks —
Rafael
